The kennel attendant on desk cover
This section outlines what the desk expects
Companion Animal Travel Desk Operations

This section governs routine desk handling for live-animal bookings, check-in support, and handoff to flight and ground teams. The desk keeps animal travel orderly, calm, and fully documented from acceptance through arrival.

Staff must review each booking for completeness, confirm that the animal is permitted for the planned service, and record any special handling notes in clear language. The desk must treat every traveler with steady courtesy and every animal with patient attention. Care plans must reflect species, temperament, and comfort needs, and the desk must pass those plans without delay to the cabin team and the welcome team.

When accepting a reservation, staff must verify the carrier condition, travel readiness, and required paperwork before the animal is accepted for movement. If there is any sign of distress, unsafe containment, or mismatch between the booking and the animal presented, the desk must pause acceptance and escalate the matter at once. The desk does not make assumptions about an animal's behavior. It records observed facts, keeps discussion brief, and avoids promises that cannot be supported by the operation.

During check-in and departure flow, the desk maintains a calm front counter, keeps the traveler informed of the next step, and confirms that the animal is prepared for transfer. The cabin team monitors animals during flight, and the desk must ensure the transfer notes are legible and complete before the animal leaves the counter area. The welcome team prepares passengers for boarding, and the desk must align its handoff with that flow so there is no confusion at the point of movement.

If a traveler arrives with an unlisted item, a changed carrier, or an animal that appears unwell, the desk must contact the senior coordinator immediately and hold the case for direction. The same applies when the booking shows a conflict between route conditions and the animal's needs. Staff should keep the traveler informed, remain respectful, and avoid debate at the counter.

All records must be entered promptly, kept accurate, and reviewed before release from the desk. Questions, exceptions, and unusual handling concerns must be directed to the senior coordinator or the operations supervisor.
